name: SQLCipher
tagline: SQLite with transparent 256-bit AES encryption of the whole database file.
description: SQLCipher is a fork of SQLite from Zetetic that encrypts every page of the database file with AES-256 and authenticates pages with HMAC, so a stolen device or backup yields nothing readable without the key. Apart from the key pragmas it behaves like SQLite, with the same SQL, file format semantics and tooling. It is the standard answer when mobile or desktop apps must encrypt local data at rest, and libraries such as Room, PowerSync and many Flutter plugins can use it. The Community Edition is BSD-licensed. Commercial editions add prebuilt packages, performance work and FIPS-validated crypto.

pricing.notes: Community Edition is free; Commercial and Enterprise editions add packaged builds, speedups, FIPS and support.

scale.notes: Same single-file limits as SQLite, with a modest encryption overhead.

strengths: Whole-file AES-256 encryption with per-page HMAC tamper detection
Full SQLite feature set and SQL compatibility
Widely integrated in mobile frameworks and sync SDKs
Long track record in password managers and regulated apps
weaknesses: Key management is your problem; a weak or hard-coded key defeats the purpose
Encryption adds CPU overhead, most noticeable on large scans
Prebuilt binaries for some platforms require a commercial license
useCases: Encrypting local data in healthcare, finance and enterprise mobile apps
Password managers and secure note apps
Desktop apps storing sensitive data offline
notIdealFor: Cases where OS-level disk encryption is already sufficient
